audit_findings.title: The valuation may mix pre-spin earnings with post-spin shares and balance sheet
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $4.0 billion gross and $3.857 billion net cash distribution; $2.0 billion share repurchase; $2.0 billion debt repayment; BDX shareholders received 39.2% of combined Waters
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 anchor OE includes separated operations, while shares and the cash/debt bridge are post-spin; the distributed Waters interest is omitted
audit_findings.evidence: When the RMT transaction is complete, BD’s Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions businesses will be spun-off to BD shareholders and simultaneously merged with a wholly owned subsidiary of Waters.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possibility: the transaction closed February 9, 2026. The model overstates continuing BDX earnings by retaining the separated businesses, but understates the total pre-transaction shareholder claim by omitting the Waters shares. The filed transaction amounts are large relative to the $49.943 billion base equity value and can change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2025 OE on the filed continuing-operations perimeter, reconcile the $3.857 billion net distribution through the $2 billion repurchase and debt repayment, use post-transaction diluted shares, and separately value the Waters shares if the intended claim includes them.

audit_findings.title: Multi-year litigation payments may be an unmodeled claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $1.6 billion accrual at June 30, 2026; computed $5.76 per valuation share and 3.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: uncovered settlement and defense payments must reduce projected OE when paid or be deducted as an equity-bridge claim
audit_findings.evidence: Amounts payable pursuant to the settlement agreement that was consummated in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024 to resolve the vast majority of the Company’s hernia litigation are included within its recorded accrual for this matter and will be paid out over a multi-year period.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and multi-year payment obligation are demonstrated, but omission from value is not yet demonstrated because payments could enter OE through working-capital changes. The $5.76-per-share gross exposure exceeds the $4.90 difference between base value and market price, so any substantial uncovered amount omitted from forecast cash flows can change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the accrual payment schedule and expected insurance recoveries, trace settlement payments through the OE working-capital calculation, and rerun with the present value of only the uncovered payments not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Temporary tax holidays may be capitalized as permanent earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $435 million FY2025 annual tax benefit; computed 12.4% of $3.5042 billion anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: holiday expirations increase cash taxes, reducing explicit-period and terminal OE
audit_findings.evidence: The tax holidays expire at various dates through 2039.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 benefit and expirations through 2039 are demonstrated. It is not established that the full $435 million disappears at once, but mechanically growing the tax-advantaged anchor through the terminal period can capitalize a benefit equal to 12.4% of anchor OE and materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Map the filed $435 million benefit by jurisdiction and expiry date, model each cash-tax step-up, and rerun the terminal value using a sustainable post-holiday tax rate.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded pension position may not be captured by annual pension expense
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $371 million unfunded position; computed $1.34 per valuation share and 0.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: an uncovered funding deficit would reduce projected OE through contributions or be deducted as a claim in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: We have significant net pension and other postretirement and postemployment benefit obligations and costs that are measured using actuarial valuations, which include assumptions for the discount rate and the expected return on plan assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The deficit is demonstrated, but the filing says no significant required fiscal-2026 contributions were anticipated and the spin-off did not materially affect benefit obligations. Even treating the entire $371 million as an additional equity claim reduces the $179.84 base value by only about $1.34 per share, insufficient by itself to change the stated scenario or buy-below conclusions.
audit_findings.action: Confirm subsequent funded status and contribution requirements; rerun only if forecast contributions are excluded from OE or the uncovered deficit increases materially.

audit_findings.title: Known FY2026 tariff costs may require a step-down before applying growth
audit_findings.mechanism: recurring tariffs reduce post-anchor operating margins and OE before scenario growth is applied
audit_findings.evidence: Based upon the latest published tariffs that are currently in effect, we expect tariffs to adversely impact our operating expense for fiscal year 2026 and potentially beyond, primarily relating to any products (or components) imported from countries across our global supply chain which have no exemption opportunities.
audit_findings.explanation: The adverse FY2026 tariff impact is demonstrated, including an actual third-quarter effect, but the filings do not isolate its amount from labor, remediation and other margin pressures. The record therefore cannot establish materiality, although starting every scenario from untariffed FY2025 OE may overstate value if the recurring cost is not embedded in growth assumptions.
audit_findings.action: Use full-year FY2026 continuing-operations results or management's quantified gross tariffs, refunds and sustainable mitigation, establish post-tariff OE, and rerun all scenarios from that level.

audit_findings.title: Factoring and supplier finance may distort owner-earnings working capital
audit_findings.magnitude: computed FY2025 balance increases of $135 million for factored receivables and $122 million for supplier finance, totaling $257 million or 7.3% of anchor OE; filed receivables transferred were $1.560 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: factoring can reduce reported receivables and supplier finance can increase payables, creating financing-driven working-capital cash inflows in OE
audit_findings.evidence: Over the normal course of its business activities, the Company transfers certain trade receivable assets to third parties under factoring agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: It is not demonstrated that the OE calculation captured these balances incorrectly, and gross factoring volume is not itself an earnings benefit. However, the disclosed year-end increases provide a potential $257 million working-capital uplift—7.3% of anchor OE—which is reasonably capable of changing value if treated as recurring operating cash generation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 receivables and payables before factoring and supplier-finance effects, trace the $257 million balance expansion through the OE calculation, normalize any financing-driven benefit, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: filed/computed FY2024 residual $142 million, equal to 4.0% of the FY2025 anchor; FY2025 amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: eligible non-economic D&A would be added back to OE and increase operating value
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $64.0m (5.7% of filed D&A); FY2017 $191.0m (17.6% of filed D&A); FY2018 $123.0m (6.2% of filed D&A); FY2019 $123.0m (5.5% of filed D&A); FY2020 $124.0m (5.8% of filed D&A); FY2021 $139.0m (6.1% of filed D&A); FY2022 $127.0m (5.7% of filed D&A); FY2023 $127.0m (5.6% of filed D&A); FY2024 $142.0m (6.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative exclusion is demonstrated, but no evidence establishes that any residual component qualifies for an add-back, and no FY2025 residual is supplied. The latest quantified residual is large enough that classification could matter, but present materiality cannot be established. This issue can only understate, not overstate, the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 D&A composition, identify residual depreciation or amortization that meets the owner-earnings add-back rule, and rerun only for the evidenced eligible amount.
